([[Chicago Heights, Illinois]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2014–2016) | draft_year = 2016 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 34 | draft_team = [[Phoenix Suns]] | career_start = 2016 | career_end = 2020 | career_number = 8, 0 | career_position = [[Point guard]] | coach_start = 2024 | years1 = {{nbay|2016|start}}–{{nbay|2017|end}} | team1 = [[Phoenix Suns]] | years2 = 2016 | team2 = →[[Northern Arizona Suns]] | years3 = {{nbay|2018|start}} | team3 = [[Chicago Bulls]] | years4 = 2018 | team4 = →[[Windy City Bulls]] | years5 = 2019–2020 | team5 = [[Stockton Kings]] | cyears1 = 2024–present | cteam1 = [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (assistant) | highlights = * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2016 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2016]]) * [[Bob Cousy Award]] (2016) * [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] ([[2015–16 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2016]]) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Defensive Player of the Year (2016) * First-team All-SEC (2016) * SEC All-Freshman Team ([[2014–15 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2015]]) * [[SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] MVP ([[2016 SEC men's basketball tournament|2016]]) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014]]) }} '''Tyler Ulis''' (born January 5, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is currently an assistant coach at the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|University of Arkansas]]. He played college basketball at the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|University of Kentucky]]. In 2015, he led his team in [[Assist (basketball)|assists]], made the 2015 SEC All-Freshman Team, and led the [[2014–15 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2014–15 Kentucky team]] that won its first 38 games before losing to [[2014–15 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] in the final four of the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2015 NCAA tournament]]. As a sophomore, Ulis was a Consensus first-team [[2016 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and earned the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Southeastern Conference Player of the Year]] and SEC Defensive Player of the Year recognition.{{Cite web |url=https://2kmtcentral.com/17/players/7220/tyler-ulis |title=Tyler Ulis (66) - MyTEAM Bronze Card - 2KMTCentral |access-date=May 6, 2019 |archive-date=May 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190506100239/https://2kmtcentral.com/17/players/7220/tyler-ulis |url-status=live }} He played for [[Marian Catholic High School (Illinois)|Marian Catholic High School]] in [[Chicago Heights, Illinois]]. He was selected to play in both the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014 McDonald's All-American Game]] and the 2014 [[Jordan Brand Classic]]. As a high school junior, he was a first team All-state selection, but he was overlooked by most top scouts until after his junior year of high school due to his height. ==Early life== Ulis was born in [[Southfield, Michigan]] (a Detroit suburb), and lived in [[Lima, Ohio]], with his mother and younger brother, Ahron.{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/video-ahron-ulis-younger-brother-of-kentucky-guard-is-turning-heads-as-eighth-grader|title=VIDEO: Ahron Ulis, younger brother of Kentucky guard, is turning heads as eighth grader|access-date=August 15, 2016|date=September 22, 2015|work=[[USA Today]]|archive-date=August 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160806050706/http://usatodayhss.com/2015/video-ahron-ulis-younger-brother-of-kentucky-guard-is-turning-heads-as-eighth-grader|url-status=live}} He ran track as a youth, competing in the [[800 metres|800 meters]] and [[1500 metres|1500 meters]]. He trained for basketball with his cousin and 2009 [[Big Ten Conference]] Defensive Player of the Year [[Travis Walton (basketball)|Travis Walton]]. Another of his cousins is Shareese Ulis, point guard for [[Cincinnati Bearcats|Cincinnati Lady Bearcats]], who had been a two-time ''[[Toledo Blade]]'' Player of the Year.{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-01-12/sports/ct-spt-0113-prep-bkb-athlete-of-month-20130112_1_preps-plus-athlete-tracy-abrams-tribune-wgn-ch|title=Tribune/WGN-Ch. 9 Athlete of the Month - Marian Catholic's Tyler Ulis|access-date=January 31, 2014|date=January 12, 2013|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Narang, Bob|archive-date=February 2, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202231748/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-01-12/sports/ct-spt-0113-prep-bkb-athlete-of-month-20130112_1_preps-plus-athlete-tracy-abrams-tribune-wgn-ch|url-status=dead}} During his time in middle school, Ulis became friends with future [[Phoenix Suns]] teammate [[Devin Booker]].{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2694797-drake-2k-and-netflix-five-moments-at-home-with-the-phoenix-suns|title=DRAKE, 2K AND NETFLIX: FIVE MOMENTS AT HOME WITH THE PHOENIX SUNS|access-date=March 6, 2017|date=February 25, 2017|work=bleacherreport.com|author=Sohi, Seerat|archive-date=March 6, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170306083537/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2694797-drake-2k-and-netflix-five-moments-at-home-with-the-phoenix-suns|url-status=live}} ==High school career== For high school, Ulis moved to [[Matteson, Illinois]], where he lived with his father, James. In Ohio, he had been used to winning a high percentage of his games. When he arrived at Marian Catholic, he started his first game as a freshman against future [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball]] starting guard [[Tracy Abrams]]. He did not initially enjoy team success. As a freshman, he was {{convert|5|ft|3|in|m|2}} tall and was being recruited by opposing high schools. He reached {{convert|5|ft|8|in|m|2}} by late in his sophomore year and began being recruited by college basketball teams.{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2012/02/02/boys-basketball-spotlight-on-marian-catholics-tyler-ulis/|title=Boys basketball - Spotlight on Marian Catholic's Tyler Ulis|access-date=January 31, 2014|date=February 2, 2012|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|archive-date=February 2, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202231615/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2012-02-02/sports/ct-spt-0203-prep-bkb-spotlight-20120202_1_boys-basketball-school-freshman-last-winter|url-status=live}} By the beginning of his junior season, Marian Catholic was regarded as a serious contender thanks to Ulis.{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2012/11/21/boys-basketball-top-5-conferences-at-a-glance/|title=Boys basketball - Top 5 conferences at a glance|access-date=January 31, 2014|date=November 21, 2012|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|archive-date=November 10, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141110192840/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2012-11-21/sports/ct-spt-1122-prep-bkb-pvw-top-5-conferences-20121121_1_jahlil-okafor-tyler-ulis-boys-basketball|url-status=live}} Because of his height, Ulis was overlooked until well into the recruiting process for top basketball schools. He was not highly recruited until his 2013–14 senior year of high school. Among schools regarded as high-major programs, only [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] and [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]] made him offers during his junior year.{{cite web|url=http://www.highschoolcubenews.com/news_article/show/344112?referrer_id=599124|title=Henricksen: Okafor, Alexander and Ulis took different paths to McDonald's game|access-date=January 31, 2014|date=January 29, 2014|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Henricksen, Joe|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140204041151/http://www.highschoolcubenews.com/news_article/show/344112?referrer_id=599124|archive-date=February 4, 2014}} His other offers were from [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]], [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]], [[Loyola Ramblers men's basketball|Loyola]], [[Northern Illinois Huskies men's basketball|Northern Illinois]] and [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2013/01/31/boys-hoops-blog-ulis-stands-pat-as-stock-soars/|title=Boys hoops blog - Ulis stands pat as stock soars|access-date=February 1, 2014|date=January 31, 2013|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|archive-date=February 2, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202231904/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-01-31/sports/ct-spt-0201-prep-bkb-helfgot-blog-20130131_1_tyler-ulis-james-ulis-tom-izzo|url-status=live}} During his junior season, his stock soared and Marian Catholic started winning.
